title: Three-step guided intake with minimum-detail validation

history.detail: CONDITIONAL: QA1 static audit, sprint 3, round 1. Verdict CONDITIONAL. Audited commit fb56cac, tree f6c02ca194df25890f03e9e2bbb367f4f2118017, working tree clean. Sprint file read in full, fresh, immediately before recording. THE TYPE SPLIT -- THE RISKY HALF OF THIS SPRINT -- IS CLEAN. VERIFIED, NOT READ. Req 10 / ACs: ConcernCategory now holds exactly the four INTAKE concerns (medical-absence, schedule-flexibility, interpersonal-conflict, performance-management). FactPatternTag holds exactly the four LEGAL patterns. Zero overlap between the two vocabularies -- checked as a set intersection, not by eye. CaseExcerpt.factPatternTags retyped to FactPatternTag[]. Req 10 / AC: data/seed-library.json is UNCHANGED by this diff (git diff --stat empty). Done as a retype, not a migration, exactly as required. Track H is unaffected. Req 10 / AC: seed-library-schema.ts retyped to Record. I proved the exhaustiveness check still bites the way AC 82 specifies -- added a fifth member to the FactPatternTag union in a copy of the real lib/types.ts, compiled the schema's exact construction against it: error TS1360: Property '"newly-added-pattern"' is missing ... but required in type 'Record' Both schema enums still match their unions exactly: 4/4 fact patterns, 15/15 grounds in order. Every tag in the shipped seed data is still a member of both enums. Req 10 / AC: Sprint 2's two test files are entirely UNMODIFIED -- not merely "unmodified except for the rename." They reference CaseExcerpt and string literals, never ConcernCategory by name, so the retype needed no edit. Loader and guard have no behavioural change. Full suite 11/11 across 4 files. Req 11: IntakeMetadata finalized with employmentStatus / tenure / formalComplaintsLodged, and the "Stubbed" note is gone from its doc comment. Req 12 / AC: lib/types.ts changes are BOUNDED. The only edits are the ConcernCategory redefinition, the new FactPatternTag, the new EmploymentStatus (a supporting closed set for requirement 11, the same pattern as Sprint 1's ProceduralCheckStatus), the IntakeMetadata finalization, the CaseExcerpt.factPatternTags retype, and one stale doc comment reference. No other domain type changes shape. Not a FAIL. AC: no locally declared domain type anywhere in the diff. The two local declarations are `type Step = 1|2|3` (UI state) and `ValidationResult` (a mechanism result shape, the same class as Sprint 2's CitationGuardResult, which passed). No Pick<>/Omit<> anywhere. AC: no intake component references a legal fact pattern -- grepped app/ and components/ for all four legal values and for FactPatternTag. Zero hits. The bridge is left to Sprints 4 and 5, as required. OTHER REQUIREMENTS MET Req 1: three steps, visible "Step N of 3" plus a progress list; all state lives in the parent so Back preserves entered data by construction, not by save/restore logic. Req 2/3/4: all specified fields and all three distinct narrative prompts present. Req 5: MIN_NARRATIVE_LENGTH = 100, single named export, with a comment that actually explains the number and admits it is a starting value. Exactly what was asked. Req 8: every input has a label -- tenure and all three textareas use useId()+htmlFor, radios and checkboxes are wrapped in

PASS: QA1 static audit, sprint 3, round 2. Verdict PASS.
Audited commit ffe1389, tree 62a67a3a48f9de55bde7672221242da4feb86a8b, working tree clean.
Sprint file re-read IN FULL, fresh, immediately before recording -- it changed this round
(Amendment 2 added requirements 13-15), hash
bce74e68e0774327cf277848488f6e71b4e5d13e65a554601df6d5f8aaff9ef9.

ALL FOUR ROUND-1 FINDINGS FIXED.

1. Step 1 generic message -- FIXED. goToStep2 now accumulates the missing fields and
   reports "Missing: employment status, length of employment." Requirement 6 satisfied at
   step 1, which was the one place it slipped.
2. Empty strings in Situation.facts -- FIXED, and fixed better than I proposed. I suggested
   filtering the empties. Amendment 2 requirement 14 went the other way and kept all three
   entries while making the distinction type-level, which is the correct call: filtering
   would have destroyed exactly the information Sprint 5 needs. My round-1 recommendation
   is superseded and the superseding design is better.
3. Silent return on submit -- FIXED. The unreachable-guard branch now sets an explicit
   message pointing back to steps 1 and 2, with a comment recording why it is currently
   unreachable and why it is surfaced anyway (Sprint 7 step-jumping/resume). Exactly the
   fix requested.
4. Non-empty tuple defeated by a cast -- FIXED. `as [ConcernCategory, ...]` is gone;
   `const [firstConcern, ...restConcerns] = concerns` then `[firstConcern, ...restConcerns]`
   infers the tuple type structurally. No assertion remains on that path.

AMENDMENT 2 -- ALL THREE REQUIREMENTS MET.

Req 13 (per-prompt validation): three named exported constants --
  MIN_WHAT_HAPPENED_LENGTH 100, MIN_DOCUMENTATION_LENGTH 20, MIN_EMPLOYER_ACTION_LENGTH 20 --
  each with a comment giving a real rationale, not a restatement. The differentiated values
  are reasoned rather than uniform: the documentation prompt is often a short specific fact
  ("A doctor's note was requested and provided on March 3") rather than a narrative, so a
  100-char bar there would push users toward padding. The combined gate is GONE, not
  supplemented -- grepped app/, components/ and lib/ for MIN_NARRATIVE_LENGTH and
  validateNarrative: zero hits.
  AC 110's specific test exists and passes (intake-validation.test.ts:39), named for the
  round-1 scenario: 100 chars in prompt one, other two empty -> prompt one valid, other two
  INVALID. The exact case the combined threshold let through.

Req 14 (type-level not-reported marker): FactPromptResponse is a genuine discriminated
  union -- { reported: true; text: string } | { reported: false }. An empty string cannot
  masquerade as "not applicable" and a not-reported entry cannot carry text; both are
  unrepresentable, not merely discouraged. Situation.facts is a fixed
  [FactPromptResponse, FactPromptResponse, FactPromptResponse] tuple -- always three, never
  filtered, positionally bound to requirement 4's three prompts. Sprint 5's three-state
  ProceduralCheckStatus is now reachable: "no documentation was exchanged" and "the employer
  skipped the question" are distinguishable, which was Amendment 2's stated reason for
  existing. toFactPromptResponse is unit-tested to return the marker with no `text` property
  at all, not an empty one.
  UI half present: a per-prompt "Nothing yet / not applicable" checkbox with its own label
  and id, disabling the textarea when checked.

Req 15 (ARIA on the validation path): role="alert" on every message container (3 sites),
  aria-describedby wiring inputs and fieldsets to their message ids (6 sites),
  aria-invalid on the failing inputs. Present across steps 1, 2 and 3, not just one.

EVERYTHING FROM ROUND 1 STILL HOLDS -- RE-VERIFIED, NOT ASSUMED
lib/types.ts changes remain bounded to requirements 10, 11 and 14. The only additions this
  round are FactPromptResponse and the Situation.facts retype, both requirement 14. No other
  domain type changed shape.
ConcernCategory 4 intake concerns / FactPatternTag 4 legal patterns, zero overlap (set
  intersection, not eye). HumanRightsCodeGround still 15.
data/seed-library.json, lib/seed-library.ts, lib/citation-guard.ts and both Sprint 2 test
  files are untouched across the ENTIRE sprint diff, not just this round. Loader and guard
  have no behavioural change of any kind.
seed-library-schema.ts unchanged since round 1, where I proved the Record<FactPatternTag,
  true> exhaustiveness check still fails to compile on an added fact pattern.
No locally declared domain type. The two local declarations are `type Step = 1|2|3` (UI
  state) and ValidationResult (a mechanism result shape, same class as Sprint 2's
  CitationGuardResult).
On AC 108's prohibition of utility-type aliases: intake-validation.ts:84 uses
  Extract<FactPromptResponse, { reported: true }> as an inline type predicate in a filter.
  This is not what that criterion forbids. It is derived from the domain type so it cannot
  drift, it names the union's own branch rather than a near-copy, and it never becomes a
  shape a component depends on -- it exists only to narrow inside toNarrative. Passes.
Suite 16/16 across 4 files. typecheck clean, lint clean.
Requirement 9's four original cases all still present and passing.

DOCUMENTATION DEFECT -- MASTER CONTROLLER CLEANUP, NOT A CODE FIX, NOT BLOCKING

Acceptance criterion line 117 still reads: "QA1 confirms the minimum-detail threshold is a
single named exported constant with an explanatory comment, not a magic number inline."
That directly contradicts AC line 110 ("three named exported constants ... and no single
combined gate remaining") and requirement 13 ("The single combined MIN_NARRATIVE_LENGTH gate
is replaced, not supplemented"). Line 117 is residue Amendment 2 forgot to strike.

I audited against requirement 13 and AC 110. Stating that explicitly because it is a
judgment about precedence, not a waiver: Amendment 2 is the later, explicit instruction and
says which way the conflict resolves, so satisfying AC 117 would require violating the
requirement written to replace it. This is not the Sprint 1 requirement-8 situation, where a
criterion was genuinely unsatisfiable with nothing superseding it and the resolution needed
a real decision. If Master Controller disagrees with my reading, the verdict changes.

Strike line 117. It matters beyond tidiness: this PASS freezes the sprint file hash with the
contradiction inside it, and Sprint 4 is the next sprint and a natural candidate for reusing
this file as a template. This is the third time an amendment has left a stale acceptance
criterion behind (Sprint 1 requirement 8, Sprint 1 AC 89, now this) -- worth a line in
CLAUDE.md's amendment guidance: an amendment that replaces a requirement must strike the
acceptance criteria that tested the old one, in the same edit.

HANDOFF WARNING
This PASS freezes the sprint file hash. /sprint-dev-done is the only command that checks it
and refuses outright if the file changed. Do not edit the sprint file -- including striking
AC 117 -- between now and /sprint-dev-done. Do it after /sprint-ship, per CLAUDE.md's timing
constraint, or before dev-done and re-run this audit.

CARRIED FORWARD FOR SPRINT 5
Situation.facts is now a positional 3-tuple of FactPromptResponse. Sprint 5's spotter must
handle `reported: false` as a distinct input state rather than treating it as absence, and
CodeGround.triggeredBy should never cite a non-reported prompt. That is the whole point of
requirement 14 and it is the first thing Sprint 5's audit should check.

VERDICT: PASS. Gate 1 clear. Dev Team may run /sprint-dev-done.
